subject: Response ladder & uptime credit escalator — MSA/Order Form coordination
messages:
From: Alicia Grant <alicia.grant@acmesolutions.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmesolutions.com
Date: Tue, 27 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Uptime credits — proposal for escalator + maintenance windows

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the MSA and order form draft. Our procurement team ran the SLA spreadsheet against our run-rate and surfaced two items we'd like to discuss before legal redlines: a) the proposed credit schedule caps out too quickly for us when incidents extend beyond short windows, and b) maintenance window language is tighter than our typical enterprise policy.

High-level asks from Acme:
- Introduce a short "credit escalator" so credit % increases with incident duration (e.g., 99.5% -> 99.0% -> 98.0% tiers) rather than a flat monthly cap immediately.
- Link credits to monthly recurring charges (MRR) rather than token-based usage for predictability.
- Allow a single 8-hour monthly maintenance window with 48h advance notice; anything beyond that should be treated as a scheduled outage with different credit calculations.

I attached a simple matrix (uptime-credit-matrix.xlsx) showing our preferred bands. Can your team confirm whether Redwood is open to an escalator approach? If so, we can route a short redline to legal. Otherwise procurement will push for a full credit removal clause.

Appreciate a quick confirmation so I can align our legal and SRE teams.

Best,
Alicia Grant
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Solutions

Attachment: uptime-credit-matrix.xlsx (excel spreadsheet, 53KB)

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Grant <alicia.grant@acmesolutions.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 May 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Uptime credits — proposal for escalator + maintenance windows

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear matrix and the ask.

Short answer: we're open to discussing an escalator-style credit schedule but need to align on caps, triggers, and governance. A few quick points from product/ops and commercial perspective:
- Redwood typically ties credits to invoice amounts (MRR) for enterprise customers, so linking to MRR is workable — we'll need to define the exact denominator (invoice for that month, trailing 30d, etc.).
- We can propose a three-tier escalator (example below) but want to cap aggregate credits per billing month to protect runway.
- Maintenance: 8h monthly with 48h notice is reasonable for standard maintenance; blackouts and emergency patches need carveouts.

Proposed escalator (draft for discussion):
- Availability >= 99.8%: no credit
- Availability 99.0% - 99.8%: 5% of MRR credit
- Availability 98.0% - 99.0%: 15% of MRR credit
- Availability < 98.0%: 30% of MRR credit, with a maximum aggregate cap of 100% of MRR in a billing month (subject to legal).

Next steps:
1) I'll loop in legal (Marissa) to do a focused redline on the Order Form/Section 4 (SLA).
2) Can we sync on a 45-min call this week with your SRE and procurement? Alicia, what times on Thu/Fri work for you?

I'll attach an internal proposal PDF and the draft redline after Marissa's first pass.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: response-ladder-proposal.pdf (draft)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, Alicia Grant <alicia.grant@acmesolutions.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 May 2025 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Uptime credits — proposal for escalator + maintenance windows

Hi all — looping in legal comments inline. I've attached a redline (ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx) with targeted edits; summary below.

Summary of legal positions (high level):
- Escalator: We can accept a stepped credit schedule but we must:
  * Preserve a monthly aggregate cap (we propose 100% of applicable MRR) to avoid open-ended liability.
  * Include a clause excluding outages caused by customer misconfiguration, third-party upstream providers (unless Redwood controls them), and Force Majeure events.
- Response ladder / priority SLA: We prefer objective response definitions (P1 = system-wide customer-impacting outage; P2 = degraded performance, etc.). We'll propose response time targets tied to support tier.
- Maintenance windows: Accept proposed 8-hour monthly window with 48h notice, but for scheduled blackouts >8h require mutual written agreement and a separate credit schedule.

Legal redline highlights (see attached):
- Section 4.2: Replace "no cap" language with "aggregate monthly cap equal to 100% of the monthly fees invoiced to Customer".
- Section 4.4: Add carveouts for customer-caused incidents and third-party outages; add examples.
- Section 5: Define response ladder table and tie response times to support plan (Standard vs. Premier).

Alicia — if you can share your SRE's definition of P1/P2 and preferred response times, we'll try to align commercial and legal wording. Otherwise, we can propose conservative defaults and allow SRE-run playbook to sit outside the MSA.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Attachment: ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx (redline, 112KB)

From: Jason Lowe <jason.lowe@acmesolutions.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Alicia Grant <alicia.grant@acmesolutions.com>, procurement@acmesolutions.com
Date: Thu, 29 May 2025 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Uptime credits — proposal for escalator + maintenance windows

Marissa / Dylan — thanks for the quick responses and the redline. A couple of counterpoints from Acme SRE and Finance:
- We understand Redwood's need for a cap, but a 100% aggregate monthly cap effectively limits our ability to recoup sustained business impact. We propose removing the hard monthly cap and instead setting a per-incident cap tied to a multiple of daily MRR (e.g., up to 300% of daily MRR per qualifying incident).
- For regional services (we have a heavy EU footprint), we need a higher baseline target for critical endpoints (99.9% for EU-facing APIs). If Redwood cannot commit globally, we ask for region-specific service levels.
- On maintenance: 8h with 48h notice is fine, but we want a guaranteed two annual blackout windows (up to 4h each) where Redwood will not schedule other maintenance — important for our engineering sprints.

On the response ladder, we prefer: P1 — 15 minute response acknowledgment, P2 — 1 hour, P3 — 4 hours. Are those feasible under your Standard/ Premier support levels?

We can take the redline and propose a clean order form once we agree on the commercial anchors. Happy to hop on Fri morning if that helps.

—Jason
Director, SRE Operations | Acme Solutions
